Australia.entity_types: Public charitable trust, company limited by guarantee (CLBG), registered association
Australia.cost_time: A$0 ACNC fee (~A$514 if incorporating a CLBG with ASIC), 1-4 weeks
Australia.requirements: Australian resident (home jurisdiction); registered office in Australia; 2+ Australian-resident trustees/directors; ABN then ACNC registration for charitable status
Australia.notes: Home setup: register with ACNC (Australian Charities and Not-for-profits Commission) for tax-deductible-gift status; most foreign-linked founders use a charitable trust with local trustees

New Zealand.entity_types: Incorporated society, company limited by guarantee, registered trust
New Zealand.requirements: Charity Commission registration (free, online); NZ-based charity board majority for tax status; no strict local-citizen rule for society incorporation
New Zealand.notes: Very straightforward English-language process; foreign founders commonly use an incorporated society with some NZ-resident officers

Fiji.entity_types: Charitable trust (registered trust), company limited by guarantee
Fiji.requirements: CLBG: 3 directors, 2 ordinarily resident in Fiji; charitable trust: 2+ trustees + local registered address; English widely used
Fiji.notes: Trusts registered with FRCS/Registrar; CLBG route is the common NGO structure; appointing two resident Fijian directors is the main hurdle

Papua New Guinea.entity_types: Non-commercial company limited by guarantee, registered association (NGO)
Papua New Guinea.requirements: Resident company secretary in PNG; 7+ members with 3+ PNG residents for non-commercial company; local registered office
Papua New Guinea.notes: Bureaucracy heavy, English official language but processes slow; most international NGOs register via a PNG partner or use an Australian-registered entity operating cross-border

Samoa.entity_types: Company limited by guarantee, registered trust
Samoa.requirements: At least 1 director resident in Samoa; local registered office/agent; 2+ trustees for a trust
Samoa.notes: Small registry, English official; foreign trustees allowed with a local resident officer; SIFA handles international structures (not for local charities)

Tonga.requirements: Resident trustee/director and local office; registration with Ministry of Justice/trust registry
Tonga.notes: Small, insular bureaucracy; limited precedent for foreign-registered charities; political sensitivity around foreign NGOs - community consent often expected

Vanuatu.entity_types: Company limited by guarantee, registered trust
Vanuatu.requirements: CLBG needs local registered office/agent; 1+ resident director recommended; English widely used
Vanuatu.notes: Relatively permissive offshore-friendly registry; post-2021 coup political risk noted by some aid donors

Solomon Islands.entity_types: Charitable trust (registered), company limited by guarantee
Solomon Islands.requirements: Charitable trusts must be registered with charitable purpose; local registered office and resident officer recommended; 2+ trustees
Solomon Islands.notes: English official, cooperative registry; foreign charitable trusts common (many Pacific-worker charities registered here); political instability occasional

Kiribati.requirements: Local registered office, resident trustee/director; small central registry in Tarawa
Kiribati.notes: Very small registry with limited published process; English official but slow administration; few foreign charity registrations on record

Nauru.requirements: Minimal corporate framework; no established charitable registration regime; local agent required for any entity
Nauru.notes: No dedicated charity register; foreign founders can only form IBC/trust via offshore service providers; not a practical charity jurisdiction

Tuvalu.requirements: Business registration effectively restricted to Tuvaluan citizens or Tuvalu-based businesses (per Ministry of Finance); local officers and office required
Tuvalu.notes: Explicit non-citizen registration restrictions; no practical foreign charity pathway; use a partner in Fiji/NZ instead

Marshall Islands.entity_types: Registered trust (trust company regime), company, LLC
Marshall Islands.requirements: Local registered agent (default: The Trust Company of the Marshall Islands, Inc.) for non-residents; no local directors required for most entities
Marshall Islands.notes: Well-developed English-language trust/registered-agent infrastructure; charitable purposes uncommon but trust structures easy to set up

Micronesia.requirements: Registration in one of 4 states (or federally) with a local registered agent; no local-citizen director requirement
Micronesia.notes: Small registries, English official; registered-agent services available; charitable framework informal - trust deed is the usual vehicle

Mongolia.cost_time: Modest state fees (tens of USD) plus notarization; typically 2–8 weeks for registration.

Japan.entity_types: General incorporated association (一般社団法人); Specified NPO (特定非営利活動法人); Unincorporated voluntary group (任意団体)
Japan.cost_time: Government fees of roughly ¥30,000–50,000 plus office costs; a general incorporated association registers in about 2–4 weeks, while Specified-NPO certification takes 3–6 months.
Japan.requirements: No nationality or residency bar — a foreign founder can serve as director — but registration requires a Japanese registered office address (serviced/registered-agent office works), Japanese-language articles, and a registered seal (hanko).
Japan.notes: The fastest expat path is the non-profit general incorporated association (can register in as little as two weeks); Specified-NPO status adds tax-deductible donation treatment but a longer, prefecture-run certification. All documents in Japanese; Eng

South Korea.entity_types: Private foundation (재단법인); Incorporated association (사단법인); Nonprofit corporation (비영리법인)
South Korea.cost_time: Low official registration fees; with a local agent typically a few weeks to ~2 months once endowment is in place.
South Korea.requirements: Foreigners are permitted to establish foundations in Korea with no director-residency requirement; registration (district/city office under the Act on Incorporation of Associations and Foundations) needs a local office address, a Korean-language cons
South Korea.notes: Confirmed viable for expats (KOTRA/Invest Korea and formation guides both confirm foreigners can register foundations and NGOs); Korean-language paperwork is the main burden; popular expat-charity route is the 재단 법인 for grantmaking.

China.entity_types: Public-interest foundation (公募基金会); Non-public-interest foundation (非公募基金会); Private non-enterprise unit (民办非企业单位)
China.cost_time: Several months to over a year including the 2-year operational-pilot requirement and approvals; official fees low, agent/legal costs significant.
China.requirements: Registration requires a Chinese supervising/competent unit (主管单位), a Chinese registered address, and a paid-in registered fund of at least 2 million RMB (public-interest foundation) or 800,000 RMB (non-public-interest); foreign individuals generally
China.notes: Direct foreign formation is effectively barred without a local Chinese partner organization; foreign-funded groups must register under the Foreign NGO Law (2+ years of overseas track record) or operate through a local partner — heavy political/superv

Taiwan.entity_types: Private foundation (財團法人); Mutual-benefit association (互益社團法人)
Taiwan.cost_time: Modest registration fees (a few hundred to a few thousand USD with legal help); typically 4–12 weeks once capital is deposited.
Taiwan.requirements: Foreigners can form a private foundation with a local registered office in Taiwan and a deposited minimum capital of 15 million NTD (local-level registration) or 30 million NTD (central-level, Ministry of the Interior); documents in Chinese, board ca
Taiwan.notes: The 財團法人 (foundation) is the standard expat charitable vehicle; formation guides confirm foreign founders are accepted and foreign staff may be hired; Chinese-language bureaucracy, no direct foreign-ownership ban.

Hong Kong.entity_types: Company limited by guarantee (no share capital); Charitable trust under deed of trust; Registered society (small member groups)
Hong Kong.cost_time: Government incorporation fees of a few hundred to ~HK$2,000; incorporation in 3–5 days; HKJC charitable registration (for donation tax deductions) takes additional 1–3 months.
Hong Kong.requirements: No nationality or residency requirement for directors/members; a Hong Kong registered office address (virtual office works) and company secretary must be in place; charity status for tax benefits is a separate application to the HK Jockey Club (HKJC)
Hong Kong.notes: The most accessible route in this list; full English-language process; popular expat pathway is the company limited by guarantee, then HKJC charitable status; low political risk.

Macau.entity_types: Private foundation (Fundação Privada, Law 16/2021, in force 2022); Association (社團, new law in force 2022)
Macau.cost_time: Notary and registration costs of a few hundred to a few thousand MOP; typically a few weeks to 2–3 months.
Macau.requirements: No nationality bar; the foundation can be established by a single founder with a donated endowment and a local office address, via the DSAJ registration process (name certificate, then incorporation with Civil Affairs Bureau); an association requires
Macau.notes: The 2021/2022 modernization (association and foundation laws) lowered formation barriers; documents in Chinese or Portuguese — English support is limited; political risk similar to Macau generally.

Singapore.entity_types: Registered charity (Registrar of Charities), company incorporated by guarantee, society
Singapore.requirements: At least one director/trustee resident in Singapore, local registered office (agent address OK), English-language constitution.
Singapore.notes: No foreign-formation ban; English-language bureaucracy; most region-friendly setup; separate IRC tax-exempt (s16/s17) and PCDU applications follow incorporation.

Malaysia.entity_types: Society (Societies Act 1966), charitable trust, company incorporated by guarantee
Malaysia.requirements: Local registered office, at least one local resident officer (company: resident director; society: Malaysian officebearers), English filings accepted.
Malaysia.notes: Society is the common expat-charity form; registration in English or Bahasa; straightforward via local secretary/agent.

Indonesia.requirements: Individual foreign founder must have resided in Indonesia 5 consecutive years; foreign board members need Ministry of Foreign Affairs recommendation; local notary deed required.
Indonesia.notes: Effectively foreigners use an Indonesian corporate (PT) or local individual as founder of record, or partner with an existing yayasan; Bahasa Indonesia dominant.

Thailand.entity_types: Foundation (Foundation Act 2007), registered NGO/society, charitable trust
Thailand.requirements: Majority of foundation board Thai nationals, local registered office, Thai-language documents, in-person notarisation steps.
Thailand.notes: Most foreigners establish a foundation with all-Thai board and act as funder/advisor; high political sensitivity (NGO rules, lèse-majesté) — avoid politically active purposes.

Vietnam.entity_types: Social charity organisation (local NGO), INGO representative office
Vietnam.cost_time: N/A for individual foreign founder (INGO route: 3–6 months)
Vietnam.requirements: Only Vietnamese social organisations can be formed; foreign individuals cannot found a local charity; INGO registration needs MFA/COMINGO approval and foreign funding source.
Vietnam.notes: Practical route is partnering with a Vietnamese social organisation or registering in Singapore; strict annual reporting; no local fundraising by INGOs.

Philippines.entity_types: Non-stock non-profit corporation (SEC), charitable trust, association
Philippines.requirements: At least two-thirds of directors of a non-stock corporation must be Filipino citizens resident in the Philippines; trust trustees likewise Filipino; local office address.
Philippines.notes: English is an official language — filings in English; popular expat hub; common structure is a Filipino-majority board with the foreigner as incorporator/trust donor.

Cambodia.entity_types: Association, NGO (Law on Associations and NGOs 2003, as amended), foundation
Cambodia.cost_time: N/A for foreign individual founder (≈USD 200 + local sponsor costs, 1–2 months if via Cambodian nationals)
Cambodia.requirements: Founding members must be Cambodian nationals; local office and national chair; annual renewal and foreign-funding registration (MOFA) for INGO activity.
Cambodia.notes: 2025 draft/NGO law further tightens controls; notable political risk and periodic clampdowns on foreign-funded NGOs; partner with local nationals as founders of record.

Laos.entity_types: Social organisation (Law on Social Organisations and NGOs), INGO representative office
Laos.cost_time: N/A for foreign individual founder (≈USD 100–300 + legal fees via local partners, 2–6 months)
Laos.requirements: Founding members must be Lao residents/nationals with a Lao national chair; local office; state registration via Ministry of Home Affairs.
Laos.notes: Heavily state-controlled civil society; Lao language required; INGOs operate only through approved local partners and MFA authorisation.

Myanmar.entity_types: Registered charity/association (National Registration Bureau), INGO representative office
Myanmar.cost_time: N/A for foreign individual founder (≈USD 100–300 via local sponsor, months if feasible)
Myanmar.requirements: Registration requires a local sponsor/contact and Burmese-language filings; foreign individuals cannot form organisations directly.
Myanmar.notes: High political risk (civil war, sanctions, unstable NCA); most foreign charities operate via international partners or pre-2021 registered bodies only.

Brunei.entity_types: Society (Societies Act), charitable trust (registered with Registrar of Societies)
Brunei.requirements: Local registered office, majority of office-bearers Bruneian citizens, in-person registry steps; no online filing.
Brunei.notes: Very small, closed registration culture aimed at locals; English is official so language is fine, but foreign-led charities are rare — most operate through existing local bodies.

Timor-Leste.entity_types: Association (2009 Law on Associations), NGO, foundation
Timor-Leste.requirements: Physical local office, registered local address and national contact officer; filings in Tetum/Portuguese/English; slow manual process.
Timor-Leste.notes: Foreign members are permitted under the 2009 law and INGOs do register here; bureaucracy is slow and requires a local agent; less predictable than Singapore/Malaysia.

India.entity_types: Public charitable trust (state trust deeds), registered society, Section 8 company (Companies Act 2013)
India.cost_time: Trust: ~INR 2,000-15,000 fees plus stamp duty, 2-6 weeks; Sec 8: ~INR 30,000-50,000, 6-12 weeks
India.requirements: Trust: 2+ trustees with at least one Indian-resident trustee in practice, Indian registered office and bank account; Sec 8 company: 1+ director resident in India 182 days/yr.
India.notes: 12A (income-tax exemption) and 80G (donor deductions) registrations are separate follow-up applications, add 1-3 months. English widely used in filings. Foreign founders routinely use trust + Indian resident trustees.

Pakistan.entity_types: Public charitable trust (trust deed), Section 21 non-profit company (Companies Act 2017), registered society
Pakistan.requirements: 2+ trustees with at least one Pakistani resident in practice, local registered office; Sec 21 company needs at least one Pakistani resident director and local secretary.
Pakistan.notes: Tax-exempt status is a separate FBR application after incorporation. English used in filings; local resident trustee/director is the main hurdle for a foreign founder.

Bangladesh.entity_types: NGO registered under the NGO Act 1961, charitable trust, registered society
Bangladesh.requirements: At least two-thirds of the NGO board must be Bangladeshi citizens (NGO Act 1961, s.3); local office and local officers required.
Bangladesh.notes: Foreign founder cannot form an NGO without enough Bangladeshi citizens to fill 2/3 of the board. The 2016 NGO Ordinance restricts foreign-funded NGOs (derogatory-remarks clause) - ongoing political/legal risk for donor-funded charities.

Sri Lanka.entity_types: Public charitable trust (registered with Registrar of Companies), society (Societies Ordinance), non-profit company
Sri Lanka.requirements: Trust deed with 2+ registered persons (3 recommended), local registered office; no citizenship requirement for trustees.
Sri Lanka.notes: Most expat-friendly in the region for a foreign founder; English is an official language. 12B tax-exempt status application to IRD follows trust registration.

Nepal.entity_types: Trust (Trust Act 2064), NGO (NGO Registration Act 2049, District Administration Office), registered society
Nepal.requirements: NGO: board of 7 with at least 5 Nepali citizens, registration at the District Administration Office plus Social Welfare Council affiliation; Trust: 1+ settlor, foreign settlor permitted.
Nepal.notes: The trust route is the simplest expat pathway (no citizen-quota for trust deed). Foreign funding requires Social Welfare Council approval, which adds time and discretion.

Bhutan.entity_types: NGO (NGO Act 2008 / NGO Trust Act 1997), trust
Bhutan.cost_time: Low fees, 2-8 weeks once a local sponsor is secured
Bhutan.requirements: Mandatory local Bhutanese sponsor/partner (FDI policy requires local partners; NGO registration requires a sponsoring agency).
Bhutan.notes: No direct foreign formation - a Bhutanese sponsor or partner organization is required. Small, tightly controlled NGO ecosystem; English used in official filings.

Afghanistan.entity_types: NGO (NGO Law 2015, NGO Registration Committee), foundation/association under the Hezb and Foundations Act
Afghanistan.cost_time: Low nominal fees, months to process; security and access risks dominate
Afghanistan.requirements: Registration through the NGO Registration Committee (Ministry of Foreign Affairs) with local offices; effective operation requires local partners and security access.
Afghanistan.notes: Severe political risk: Taliban administration since 2021, sanctions on funds to Afghanistan, widespread donor suspension. Not a practical registration venue for most foreign founders.

Maldives.entity_types: Public charitable trust (Public Trusts Act 1921, as amended, registered with MIRA), society, non-profit company
Maldives.requirements: Trust registered with MIRA (Maldives Investment and Regulatory Authority) with 3+ trustees; practical requirement of resident local trustees and a Maldivian registered office.
Maldives.notes: Most expats use the MIRA-registered public trust with local resident trustees and a local manager. English used in filings; annual returns and audited accounts required by MIRA.

Israel.entity_types: amuta (registered association), nonprofit corporation (amuta atzmit), public-benefit corporation (charitable amuta with DSD status)
Israel.requirements: 2-3 founders over 18 (Israeli citizenship NOT required), local Israeli registered agent/office, attorney-filed founding declaration and bylaws; English widely accepted
Israel.notes: One of the most foreign-friendly registration regimes in the region; most foreign founders use an amuta plus a local managing director and registered-agent service; English-language filings routinely accepted; charity tax status (DSD/13-b) is a separ

Jordan.entity_types: registered association (jam'iyya) with Ministry of Social Affairs, charitable trust (less common)
Jordan.cost_time: A$100-500 fees, 1-3 months (gated by finding 5+ Jordanian-citizen board members)
Jordan.requirements: Board members must be Jordanian citizens, 18+, fully competent; Jordanian local address; Arabic documents; foreign founder can only be a non-board supporter
Jordan.notes: Most foreigners fund through established Jordanian charities (e.g. JRC) or a branch/representative office instead of forming; government approval of bylaws and activities required; English not required in filings

Lebanon.entity_types: association (jama'iyya) under Law 92/1996, private foundation (muassasa khassisa)
Lebanon.requirements: Foreigners CAN be founders and directors (no nationality rule) but need a local registered office, Arabic founding documents, and a local signatory; notification (declaration) regime, not pre-approval
Lebanon.notes: Legally one of the easiest for foreigners in the region, but heavy Arabic-only bureaucracy, bank-account opening friction, and macro instability (currency, banking) make practical setup harder; most internationals use a local registered partner or a

Syria.entity_types: association registered with Ministry of Social Affairs and Labor, private foundation
Syria.cost_time: Nominally low fees, 1-4 months in a stable environment; currently not practically achievable remotely
Syria.requirements: Local registration, local address and signatories; new association regime post-2025 is still being implemented; in-person steps in Syria; OFAC sanctions complicate cross-border funding and US-dollar transactions
Syria.notes: Civil-society registration resumed after 2025 transition (586 NGOs registered by Feb 2025) but framework unstable; sanctions exposure for foreign founders and their banks; English support effectively unavailable; advise against direct formation

Iraq.entity_types: NGO/association (jam'iyya) under Law 12/2010, private foundation, branch of international NGO
Iraq.requirements: Founding members must be Iraqi nationals or Iraq-resident; minimum 10 founders; local board, local address; Arabic filings; activity approvals from MoSAL
Iraq.notes: Resident-expat route is the standard workaround (Iraqi-resident staff as founders); foreign funding rules restrict donor channels; English commonly understood in NGO sector but filings in Arabic; security considerations for in-person steps

Saudi Arabia.entity_types: civil society organization (association) under the 2024 Civil Society Law, branch of foreign NGO (via partnership)
Saudi Arabia.cost_time: N/A for foreign founder (formation not permitted); partnership route: several months
Saudi Arabia.requirements: At least 10 founding members, ALL Saudi citizens; Saudi board; Saudi address; no foreign-founded charities; foreigners may only join as members of an existing Saudi organization
Saudi Arabia.notes: New 2024 law (Royal Decree M/111) modernized the regime but kept the Saudi-citizenship floor; the only realistic foreign route is a program partnership with a Saudi charity or a representative office for an existing foreign NGO; English widely used i

Kuwait.entity_types: association (jam'iyya) under the NGOs Law, representative office of foreign NGO
Kuwait.cost_time: N/A for foreign founder (formation not permitted); representative-office route: 2-4 months with a local partner
Kuwait.requirements: Founders and board must be Kuwaiti citizens; local address; Arabic filings; foreign individuals cannot form an NGO
Kuwait.notes: Closed to foreign formation; foreigners work through established Kuwaiti charities (e.g. Kuwait Foundation for the Disabled, local societies) or a government-approved representative office; English usable informally, filings in Arabic

Qatar.entity_types: private charitable institution (Qatar Charity framework), branch/partnership with an existing charity
Qatar.cost_time: N/A for foreign founder (standalone formation not permitted); partnership route: 1-3 months
Qatar.requirements: Founding of a charitable institution requires Qatari citizens (Qatari chair and majority); foreign founders cannot establish a standalone charity; English filings accepted by many agencies
Qatar.notes: 2023 philanthropy law tightened state oversight of foreign-funded work; standard foreign route is a partnership with Qatar Charity or an established Doha NGO, or a representative office approved by the relevant ministry

United Arab Emirates.entity_types: private foundation (charitable) under Federal Decree-Law 11/2018, registered charity (DCC/DED charity license), association (jama'iyya) under FDL 2/2019
United Arab Emirates.cost_time: Foundation: AED 30,000-75,000 all-in (capital + fees + agent), 4-8 weeks; DCC charity registration for an existing foreign charity: AED 5,000-15,000, 4-8 weeks
United Arab Emirates.requirements: Foundation: 1-3 founders, 100% foreign ownership allowed, AED 100,000+ capital, local service provider; association: board must be at least 70% UAE nationals; local office address; English accepted
United Arab Emirates.notes: Most accessible Gulf option for a foreign founder: a UAE private foundation can be 100% foreign-held and run charitable activities; Dubai Charities (DCC) also registers existing international charities; the association route is blocked for all-foreig

Oman.entity_types: association (jama'iyya), private foundation, branch of foreign NGO
Oman.cost_time: A$200-600 fees, 1-3 months (gated by finding Omani board members)
Oman.requirements: Founders and board majority must be Omani nationals; Omani chair; local address; Arabic filings; foreign founders cannot chair
Oman.notes: Omani nationals are required for leadership roles; practical route for an Australian founder is a program partnership with an existing Omani charity or a representative office with a local sponsor; English usable in government dealings, filings in Ar

Bahrain.entity_types: association (NGO) under Law 19/2006, branch of international NGO
Bahrain.cost_time: A$200-500 fees, 4-8 weeks (gated by Bahraini board)
Bahrain.requirements: Founders must be Bahraini citizens (min. ~20) and board must be at least two-thirds Bahraini; local address; Arabic filings
Bahrain.notes: Bahrain is the most English-friendly and transparent NGO administration in the Gulf, but the nationality floor on founders/board keeps foreign formation out of reach; standard route is a partnership with an existing Bahraini NGO; government relations

Yemen.entity_types: association (jama'iyya) under NGO Law 73/1991, NGO representative office (MOU-based)
Yemen.cost_time: N/A in practice; formal route nominally 1-3 months in a stable environment, not feasible given the conflict
Yemen.requirements: Registration with Ministry of Social Affairs, local address and local signatories; in-person steps; operating environment requires MOU with authorities
Yemen.notes: Civil war, fragmented governance, sanctions (Yemen Sanctions) and funding restrictions make direct foreign formation impractical; all foreign work runs through humanitarian MOUs with recognized authorities and established local partners; advise again

Palestine.entity_types: registered society (jam'iyya) under the 1996 Societies Law, private foundation, branch of international NGO
Palestine.cost_time: A$150-500 fees, 2-6 weeks in a normal environment; occupation/sanctions add friction
Palestine.requirements: Minimum ~15 founders, two-thirds Palestinian residents of the area; local (Ramallah/West Bank) address; board majority local; Arabic filings; MoSAL registration in person
Palestine.notes: No local-partner requirement to register, so foreign participation in a society is legally possible, but in-person registration in Ramallah, movement/sanctions friction (OFAC Palestinian Territory guidelines) and banking constraints dominate; most fo

Turkey.cost_time: US$500–1,500 with a Turkish lawyer, ~1–3 months
Turkey.requirements: Foreigner may found a vakıf only under legal/actual reciprocity (Australia has no treaty, so practice relies on case-by-case reciprocity finding); majority of foundation board members must be Turkey residents; a local registered office address is req
Turkey.notes: Vakıflar Genel Müdürlüğü (Foundation Directorate) handles vakıfs; dernek registration is cheaper and simpler (province governor's office, ~1 month). English paperwork accepted with sworn Turkish translation. Political/currency risk (lira volatility)

Georgia.entity_types: public benefit organization (მფარველობითი ორგანიზაცია), charitable foundation (სარგებლობის ფონდი), non-profit organization (NPO)
Georgia.cost_time: ~GEL 25 (US$9) state fee, 3–10 business days, fully online
Georgia.requirements: Single founder (any nationality), a Georgian registered address (virtual/agent addresses accepted), no minimum funding.
Georgia.notes: Registration via Public Service Development Agency portal; English-language interface and English filings accepted. Most user-friendly regime on this list; popular with foreigners. Watch 2024–25 political instability — no effect on registration itsel

Armenia.cost_time: Minimal state fee (~600 AMD, under US$2), ~10–15 business days
Armenia.requirements: Foreign citizens may found NGOs; a local (Yerevan/Armenian) registered office is required; documents in Armenian (or Russian, widely accepted in practice).
Armenia.notes: Registration via public services (e-gov) system; apostille/translation of foreign documents needed. Post-2020 South Caucasus realignment has not tightened NGO law; Armenia is one of the more open CIS-adjacent jurisdictions for foreigners.

Azerbaijan.cost_time: State fee modest (~1,000 AZN equivalent), but real-world processing 1–3+ months with high rejection risk
Azerbaijan.requirements: Foreign citizens may formally be founders of a fond, but all board/officer control must be locally resident; August 2025 amendments prohibit banking operations with foreign financial sources for NGOs and add heavy fines, effectively barring foreign-f

Kazakhstan.entity_types: public association (қоғамдық бірлестік / IiO non-profit partnership), foundation (қор)
Kazakhstan.cost_time: Small state fee (~500–2,000 KZT), 5–10 business days via single-window registration
Kazakhstan.requirements: Foreign citizens can be founders (foreign legal persons generally cannot); a local registered address in Kazakhstan is required; filings in Kazakh (Russian accepted in practice).
Kazakhstan.notes: Registration with the Justice Committee/region. Kazakhstan's 2023 NGO reform simplified formation, but annual reporting and foreign-funding reporting obligations are strict. A Mongolian dual citizen faces no special preference — treated as a foreign

Uzbekistan.entity_types: public organization (jamoat birligi), charitable foundation (xayriya jamg'armasi)
Uzbekistan.cost_time: Near-zero state fee, ~5 business days via one-stop window (2023 reform)
Uzbekistan.requirements: Uzbek citizens must constitute a core of founders (a sole foreign founder is generally not acceptable for a jamoat birligi; a foundation allows a foreign founder with local participation); local registered office required; Uzbek-language filings.
