Turkmenistan.entity_types: public organization (köpagalyam birleşigi) — government-established only in practice
Turkmenistan.requirements: NGOs can only be created with the explicit approval of the relevant state organ; there is no independent NGO registration path and no mechanism for a foreigner to found one.
Turkmenistan.notes: Turkmenistan effectively has a state monopoly on civil society; no functioning independent charity sector, no English-language process, and no published cost/time. Not a viable jurisdiction for this founder; do not invest time here.

Tajikistan.cost_time: Small state fee (~US$50–100), ~30 days, plus travel
Tajikistan.requirements: Foreign citizens may be founders, but registration is in-person in Dushanbe (Ministry of Justice), requires Tajik/Russian-language documents, a local legal address, and notarized/apostilled paperwork.
Tajikistan.notes: Bureaucratic, Russian/Tajik-heavy process with no e-filing; NGOs operate under a restrictive environment (post-2024 crackdowns on civil society, 'foreign agent'-style pressure). Realistic only with a local law firm handling the file; political risk i

Kyrgyzstan.entity_types: charitable fund (ылайыктуу фонд / karyte fund), public organization, association (assotsiatsiya)
Kyrgyzstan.cost_time: State duty ~2,000 KGS (US$22), ~5 business days, e-filing via State Registration Portal
Kyrgyzstan.requirements: A fund can be founded by a single person of any nationality; a local registered address (agent addresses work); filings in Kyrgyz (Russian accepted; English with translation in practice).
Kyrgyzstan.notes: One of the easiest CIS registrations for a foreigner — a single-founder charitable fund with no local citizen requirement. Annual reporting and a local bank account required. Political volatility (2020, 2024) has not touched basic NGO registration la

Iran.entity_types: non-governmental organization (tashkilat-e ghayre-hozoumi / NGO), public-benefit association (ettehadiye-ye khedmat-e ghalbeye mardom)
Iran.cost_time: Nominal state fee; process 6–12+ months with a near-certain refusal for a foreigner
Iran.requirements: Registration requires Ministry of Interior (and relevant ministry) approval under the 2005 NGO Law; in practice, only Iranian nationals with an aligned political/religious profile are approved, and a foreign founder's application is not a viable path
Iran.notes: All organizations must be compatible with the constitution and 'the tenets of the Islamic Republic'; independent civil society is heavily restricted and monitored (2024–25 further crackdowns). International sanctions (US/EU) make banking and funding

Egypt.entity_types: Association (Jam'iyya, Law 84/2014), private charitable institution (Law 149/2014), nonprofit company
Egypt.cost_time: EGP 1,000–5,000 (~US$20–100) + legal/agent fees, 3–6 months incl. security vetting
Egypt.requirements: Local registered office, Egyptian-national founders/chair in practice, ministry (Youth & Sports / Social Solidarity) approval, Arabic documents.
Egypt.notes: Heavy bureaucracy and security review; Arabic mandatory; many foreign-supported charities operate via local partner bodies or branches.

Sudan.cost_time: ~US$100–300, 3–6 months, largely suspended due to conflict
Sudan.requirements: Sudanese founders/chair, local office, Ministry of Culture & Information approval.
Sudan.notes: 2023 civil war has paralysed registration bodies in most areas; acute security risk for foreign personnel; effectively unworkable right now.

Libya.requirements: Libyan-national founders/chair, local office, ministry approval; registry split between rival governments in Tripoli and the east.
Libya.notes: Fragmented dual-government structure, militia influence, no workable foreign-formation path; foreign NGOs operate via UN/embassy channels only.

Algeria.requirements: Local registered office, Arabic founding documents, declaration to the wilaya (provincial) authority; foreign founders heavily restricted.
Algeria.notes: Strict regulation with security vetting for any foreign involvement; slow bureaucracy; Arabic required.

Tunisia.requirements: Registered office in Tunisia plus a local-resident representative (Tunisian, or foreigner resident in Tunisia); simple declaration to the prefecture.
Tunisia.notes: Most open civil-society law in the region; declaration-based, so registration is fast; post-2022 political centralisation adds compliance risk.

Morocco.entity_types: Association (Law 1956 on association rights), nonprofit company (SPA)
Morocco.requirements: Moroccan registered office, Arabic statutes, wilaya/provincial governor approval; foreign founders permitted.
Morocco.notes: Governor discretion can delay approvals; most expats register via a local address agent; Arabic mandatory.

Mauritania.requirements: Local registered office, meaningful local-national involvement, registration with the interior ministry; French/Arabic documents.
Mauritania.notes: Very opaque, low-information bureaucracy; few foreign-led charities operate domestically; French-language burden.

Western Sahara.entity_types: None (no independent registry; Moroccan association law applies in Moroccan-administered areas)
Western Sahara.requirements: Not available independently; the practical route is registering an association in Morocco.
Western Sahara.notes: Contested territory (Morocco vs. Polisario); no functioning independent civil-society registry; register in Morocco instead.

Ethiopia.entity_types: Ethiopian charitable organization (2021 NGO Proclamation), foreign NGO office via a local partner
Ethiopia.requirements: Ethiopian-national founders for a domestic entity; a foreign founder must work through a partner organization or as a registered foreign NGO.
Ethiopia.notes: 2021 reform liberalised funding and registration, but foreigners cannot directly form a domestic charity; security clearance applies; Amharic/English documents.

Eritrea.entity_types: None (no independent NGO law; state-controlled associations only)
Eritrea.requirements: No legal pathway for an independent foreign-founded charity.
Eritrea.notes: No legal space for independent civil society; all associations are state-controlled; high political risk.

Djibouti.requirements: Local registered office, Djiboutian-national chair/meaningful involvement, interior-ministry registration; French/Arabic documents.
Djibouti.notes: Tight, security-driven regulation in a small country; English sometimes tolerated in practice; foreign aid actors mostly work through local partners.

Somalia.entity_types: Registered charitable organization/NGO (2013 federal NGO law)
Somalia.requirements: Somali founders for a domestic entity; foreign NGOs register through embassy channel; local presence and security plan required.
Somalia.notes: Severe insecurity and fragmented federal registries (Puntland, Somaliland, South West each have their own); foreign staff face high security risk.

Somaliland.requirements: Local registered office and local partner involvement, registration with the interior/social-affairs ministry.
Somaliland.notes: De facto state without international recognition: banking, sanctions-compliance and repatriation risk; the civil-society registry is relatively functional and stable.

South Sudan.entity_types: Registered NGO (2009 NGO Act, amended 2018), domestic association
South Sudan.requirements: South Sudanese founders for a domestic entity; foreign NGOs register via embassy channel; local office required.
South Sudan.notes: Post-conflict, high security risk, weak institutions; most international actors work through established partners or missions.

Seychelles.entity_types: Non-profit organization (Non-Profit Organizations Act 2013), public-benefit foundation, non-profit limited company
Seychelles.requirements: Local registered office and licensed local agent; foreign directors permitted; registration with the Registrar of Companies.
Seychelles.notes: English-language, simple, offshore-friendly regime; popular with foreign founders; a Seychelles charity gains no local tax-exempt status without local operations.

Mauritius.entity_types: Non-profit organization (NPO Act 2003), IFSA non-profit foundation, non-profit limited company
Mauritius.requirements: Mauritian registered office (local agent provides it); foreign founders/directors permitted; NPOs have a local-presence element.
Mauritius.notes: English-language with strong professional-services infrastructure; the IFSA foundation is the most foreigner-friendly route; popular expat-charity pathway.

Nigeria.entity_types: company limited by guarantee (CAC), trust (deed), NGO (NCMM-registered)
Nigeria.requirements: CAC registration of a company limited by guarantee with local resident directors/office, then registration with the NCMM (Nigerian Committee on Foreign Non-Governmental Organizations) and a Ministry of Interior Operational Readiness Certificate if re
Nigeria.notes: Most structured path in West Africa but multi-layered; NCMM registration and ORC are the foreigner bottlenecks; English language; strong expat NGO sector in Lagos/Abuja

Ghana.entity_types: company limited by guarantee, registered charity (Charities Commission, Act 1035 of 2020), trust
Ghana.requirements: Charitable purpose with objects meeting the Charities Act test; Ghana Charities Commission registration; Ghana-located principal office (directors may be foreign)
Ghana.notes: Most foreigner-friendly framework in the list: no local-national director requirement under the Companies Act 2019 (Act 992); Charities Commission registration has been operational since ~2021; English language

Côte d'Ivoire.entity_types: association déclarée, fondation, organisation non gouvernementale (ONG)
Côte d'Ivoire.requirements: Associations formed by declaration at the préfecture (Law n° 2022-443 of 15 Aug 2022 on OSCs) with local office; foreign-funded NGOs also need authorization from the Ministry of the Interior
Côte d'Ivoire.notes: 2022 OSC law modernized the regime (declaration for associations, authorization for foreign-funded NGOs); French-only bureaucracy; Abidjan has active local law firms that handle expat NGO setups

Benin.requirements: Declaration filed at the Direction de l'Administration Générale et des Cultes (Law n° 2015-04/PRB of 30 Jan 2016 on NGOs); local registered office; no local-national officer requirement
Benin.notes: One of the more open, stable regimes in francophone West Africa; French-only; Cotonou has NGOs/lawyers familiar with expat filings

Togo.requirements: Declaration/authorization of an association under Law n° 2000-17 of 11 Aug 2000 on NGOs; local registered office; French-language documents
Togo.notes: Administrative practice varies by préfecture; some steps in practice require in-person filing at the Mairie or prefecture in Lomé; French-only

Burkina Faso.requirements: Prior government authorization under Law n° 014/1997-AN on associations; a 2018 constitutional amendment bars NGOs that receive foreign funding above a threshold from operating
Burkina Faso.notes: High political risk: 2018 constitutional ban on foreign-funded NGOs, 2022–2025 military rule, repeated suspensions of international NGOs (e.g. 2023–24 expulsions); effectively impractical for a foreign-funded charity

Mali.entity_types: association (loi 01-019 du 20 juin 2001), organisation non gouvernementale (ONG)
Mali.requirements: Association registration with the Direction de l'Administration Générale (Law n° 2001-019); local office; French-language filings; authorization regime for foreign-funded NGOs in practice
Mali.notes: Political instability (2020–2024 coups, ongoing conflict); security situation in many regions makes on-ground operations difficult; Bamako filings are French-only

Guinea.entity_types: association (loi L/2010/004 du 3 janv 2010), organisation non gouvernementale (ONG)
Guinea.requirements: Declaration of an association under Law L/2010/004; local registered office in Conakry; French-language documents
Guinea.notes: 2010 association law uses a declaration regime (more open than the old authorization system); French-only; military rule since 2021 adds some political risk but NGO sector remains active

Guinea-Bissau.requirements: Registration of an association under Lei n.º 5/VI/96 de 21 de Dezembro de 1996 (regime de registo); local office; Portuguese-language filings
Guinea-Bissau.notes: Repeated military coups (7 since independence), fragile state capacity, weak enforcement of registrations; Portuguese (not French) documents; practical operations very difficult

Senegal.entity_types: association déclarée (décret-loi de 1965, modèle 1901), organisation non gouvernementale (ONG)
Senegal.requirements: Simple declaration of an association at the Direction de l'Action Sociale (1965 decree, French 1901 model); local registered office; French-language documents
Senegal.notes: Stable, well-established association culture; declaration regime is the easiest in francophone West Africa; 2022/2023 framework on foreign-funded NGOs (OSC law) adds a reporting layer for foreign funders; French-only

Gambia.entity_types: society (Societies Act, Cap 303), company limited by guarantee
Gambia.requirements: Registration of a society with the Registrar of Societies under the Societies Act 1972 (or Companies Act 1964 for a CLG); local office; English-language filings
Gambia.notes: English language, stable democracy; 2022 NGO Bill has been in draft years without enactment, so the old 1972 Societies Act still applies; Banjul filings manageable with a local agent

Sierra Leone.entity_types: company limited by guarantee (Companies Act 2013), trust, charitable society
Sierra Leone.requirements: Registration of a non-profit company limited by guarantee with the Companies Registry; local registered office; English-language documents
Sierra Leone.notes: English language; 2022 NGO Bill pending, so existing NGO/charitable-society registration practices continue; Freetown has expat-friendly law firms; registry throughput is slower than Ghana

Liberia.entity_types: non-governmental organization (NGO Act 2015), limited liability company (non-profit), trust
Liberia.requirements: NGO registration under the NGO Act of 2015 (Act No. 11 of 2015) with a local principal officer, local office, and a US$150 (local) fee; three-year permit renewal cycle
Liberia.notes: English language; the 2015 Act is the operative law (it replaced the older NGO Bill regime); permits must be renewed every 3 years; local principal officer requirement is the main hurdle for a fully foreign board

Niger.entity_types: association (loi 93-010 du 28 avril 1993), organisation non gouvernementale (ONG)
Niger.requirements: Registration of an association with the Direction de l'Administration Générale under Law 93-010; local registered office; French-language filings; practical authorization hurdles for foreign-funded NGOs
Niger.notes: Military rule since 2023; security situation in the north (Sahel conflict); Niamey filings are French-only; some discretionary elements in approvals

Cameroon.entity_types: association loi (registered association); ONG agréée (accredited NGO)
Cameroon.requirements: Foreign NGO requires prior Ministry of Interior authorization, a local legal representative and local office; filings in French.
Cameroon.notes: 2017 civil-society law; heavy discretionary approval; most expats partner with an existing Cameroonian association instead.

Central African Republic.requirements: Government authorization for foreign associations, local representative and local office; filings in French.
Central African Republic.notes: Conflict-affected with weak administration; security risk for on-ground work; few foreign NGOs operate legally.

Chad.entity_types: association loi; ONG agréée (2017 NGO law)
Chad.requirements: Foreign NGO needs prior Ministry of Interior approval, resident legal representative and local office; filings in French.
Chad.notes: 2017 NGO law replaced the 1967 framework; political instability since 2020; approval is slow and discretionary.

Republic of the Congo.requirements: Ministry of Interior accreditation (agrément) plus local legal representative and local office for foreign NGOs; filings in French.
Republic of the Congo.notes: French-language bureaucracy; accreditation is discretionary; stable enough for a registered agent/representative to work.

Congo (DRC).requirements: Congolese national legal representative is mandatory; foreign NGO approval from Ministry of Interior; local office.
Congo (DRC).notes: Slow and heavily scrutinized; security risk in the east; most expats work through an established local partner.

Gabon.requirements: Ministry of Interior accreditation, local legal representative and local office; filings in French.
Gabon.notes: French-language process; post-2023 political transition adds uncertainty to approvals.

Equatorial Guinea.requirements: Foreign NGO authorization from Ministry of Interior, local representative and local office; filings in Spanish/French.
Equatorial Guinea.notes: Highly centralized regime; approval is slow and discretionary; narrow civil-society space; Spanish (and French) bureaucracy.

Sao Tome & Principe.requirements: Foreign NGO authorization, local representative and local office; filings in Portuguese/French.
Sao Tome & Principe.notes: Very small, under-resourced administration; slow processing; few registered foreign NGOs; French/Portuguese required.

Rwanda.entity_types: NGO registered with MIDRRP (national NGO or foreign NGO)
Rwanda.requirements: Foreign NGO needs 2+ years' existence abroad, a local partner and Rwandan legal representative; Rwandan majority board for national NGOs.
Rwanda.notes: Strict, well-enforced 2016 NGO Act; English/French/Kinyarwanda; many expats operate through Rwandan partners rather than foreign registration.

Burundi.requirements: Prior approval from the Ministry of State for Humanitarian Affairs, local representative and local office; filings in French.
Burundi.notes: Multiple foreign NGOs have been expelled; very high political risk; approvals are discretionary and often denied.

Uganda.entity_types: NGO/CSO (local NGO or foreign NGO, NGO/CSO Act 2016)
Uganda.requirements: Local NGOs need a Ugandan majority board; foreign NGOs register with Ministry of Internal Affairs with a resident legal representative and must route funds via Ugandan bank accounts.
Uganda.notes: 2016 Act tightened foreign-funding rules; expats usually partner with a Ugandan-led CSO instead of foreign registration.

Tanzania.entity_types: NGO (local/foreign, NGO Act as amended); trust
Tanzania.requirements: Two-thirds Tanzanian directors (2021 amendments); foreign-funded NGOs register with the NGO Commission; local office.
Tanzania.notes: 2021 amendments tightened foreign-funding thresholds and local-content rules; English/Swahili; NGO Commission is strict.

Kenya.entity_types: registered NGO (local organization or foreign organization, NGO Act 2003)
Kenya.requirements: Foreign organizations need resident Kenyan directors, a KES 100,000 bank deposit and NGO Commission registration; local office.
Kenya.notes: English-language, well-trodden expat route; many Australians register as foreign organizations; strong NGO infrastructure.

Comoros.entity_types: association déclarée; ONG agréée (2019 NGO law)
Comoros.requirements: Foreign NGO approval from Ministry of Interior, local representative and local office; filings in French.
Comoros.notes: Small islands, limited administrative capacity; political instability (2018 coup, 2024 elections); French required.

Madagascar.requirements: Foreign NGOs accredited via Ministry of Foreign Affairs with a local legal representative and local office; filings in French.
Madagascar.notes: No local-citizenship board rule; political instability since 2023; French-language process, local agent usable.

Zambia.requirements: Local NGOs need a Zambian majority on the board; local office; English filings.
Zambia.notes: Open, English, stable; expats commonly register local NGOs with Zambian directors; straightforward process.

Malawi.requirements: Local NGOs need a Malawian majority (two-thirds) board; local office; English filings.
Malawi.notes: English-language, moderate bureaucracy; receiving foreign funds requires NGO registration.

Mozambique.entity_types: ONG nacional / ONG estrangeira (2005 NGO law)
Mozambique.requirements: Foreign NGOs register with the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, with a Mozambican legal representative and local office; filings in Portuguese.
Mozambique.notes: Portuguese-language process; a hired local manager can serve as legal representative.

Angola.entity_types: associação registada; ONG with local representative
Angola.requirements: Foreign NGO authorization from Ministry of Interior, local legal representative and local office; filings in Portuguese.
Angola.notes: Slow Portuguese-language bureaucracy; cautious approach needed for sensitive activities; few foreign charities register directly.

Botswana.requirements: Board of at least 3 members, local office and resident secretary; no citizenship restriction; English filings.
Botswana.notes: Stable, English-language; straightforward but small-bureaucracy processing times.

Namibia.entity_types: non-profit society (Societies Act); public benefit trust (Deeds Registry)
Namibia.requirements: No local-director requirement; local registered office/agent and English filings.
Namibia.notes: English, registered agents widely available; a popular route for SADC-based charities; low regulatory burden.

Zimbabwe.requirements: Local NGOs need a two-thirds Zimbabwean board; foreign NGOs register with the Ministry of Local Government with a local representative; fees in USD.
Zimbabwe.notes: Political risk and restrictions on donor funding for certain activities; English language; many NGOs operate via local partnerships.

Eswatini.requirements: Local office; registration with the Registrar of Societies plus NGO unit registration to receive foreign funds; English filings.
Eswatini.notes: Small, English-speaking; no local-director requirement; moderate small-country bureaucracy.

Lesotho.requirements: Local office; registration with the Ministry of Justice; English filings.
Lesotho.notes: Small, English-speaking; no local-director requirement; slow small-bureaucracy processing.

South Africa.entity_types: non-profit company (NPC, Companies Act); trust (Trust Property Control Act); PBO (SARS)
South Africa.requirements: No foreign restrictions; NCD online registration, local office/registered agent; English filings.
South Africa.notes: Most open route in the region; NPO/NPC + trust + PBO gives donor tax-deductibility; strong expat charity infrastructure and English.

Ireland.entity_types: Registered charity (Charity Commission for Ireland), company limited by guarantee (CRO), unincorporated charitable trust
Ireland.cost_time: CRO company ~€100 + CCI registration free; ~4–8 weeks
Ireland.requirements: Irish registered office and at least one EU-resident director/trustee; charities with income over €50k/yr must be registered with the Charity Commission for Ireland
Ireland.notes: English-language, common-law system; no nationality requirement for trustees; most overseas founders set up a company limited by guarantee with a local registered-office agent, then register the charity

United Kingdom.entity_types: Registered charity (Charity Commission England & Wales), company limited by guarantee, charitable trust
United Kingdom.cost_time: CLG at Companies House ~£12; Charity Commission registration free; ~8–12 weeks
United Kingdom.requirements: Charity must be established and managed in the UK: UK address, UK-based board control, and in practice at least one UK-resident trustee; no citizenship requirement
United Kingdom.notes: English-language, common law; the most popular expat-charity pathway; overseas individuals may be trustees provided management and control are in the UK

Iceland.entity_types: Nonprofit association (félag), foundation (stofnun), branch of foreign nonprofit (no formal 'charity' status)
Iceland.requirements: Icelandic registered address and local contact; association needs ~5 members; foundation requires ~ISK 3m endowment and Icelandic management
Iceland.notes: Documents in Icelandic; tax exemption (reykjafrjálsefni) must be applied for separately with the tax office; small bureaucracy but limited English support

Norway.entity_types: Unincorporated nonprofit association (ideell organisasjon), foundation (stiftelse), branch of foreign NGO
Norway.requirements: Norwegian address for the association (min. 3 adult members, no nationality rules); foundation needs ~NOK 1m capital and Norwegian-resident management
Norway.notes: Online via Altinn with English available; association is simple but requires a local contact; foundations have strict Norwegian-control rules

Finland.requirements: Finnish address; association needs min. 5 adult members; foundation needs €10k minimum capital, Finnish purpose, Finnish/Swedish-language operations and a Finnish-resident board
Finland.notes: Finnish-language requirement for documents and minutes; PRH bureaucracy is the main burden; foundations are hard for a foreign founder

Sweden.requirements: Swedish registered seat (säte) and min. 3 members for the association, no residency requirement; foundation needs ~SEK 250k+ and a Swedish-resident board
Sweden.notes: Straightforward online registration with Bolagsverket, English widely understood; a Swedish bank account for the entity typically requires a personal/D-number for the signatory

Denmark.requirements: Danish address, min. 2 members, registered in the CVR register; 2023 Foundation Act requires Danish-controlled foundations (Danish-resident board majority)
Denmark.notes: Association name and documents must be in Danish; CVR registration itself is easy; Danish-controlled foundation rules make the foundation route hard for a foreigner

Estonia.requirements: Estonian registered address (virtual office available); association needs min. 5 members, no nationality rules; foundation needs a small endowment (~€2,600+)
Estonia.notes: 100% online e-Business Register with English available; no local-national requirement; among the easiest jurisdictions for a foreign founder

Latvia.entity_types: Nonprofit organization (NVO, unified 2016-law form), foundation (dibinājums), religious organization
Latvia.cost_time: State fee ~€30–100 plus notary costs; ~1–2 months
Latvia.requirements: Latvian address, Latvian-language name/documents, and founding documents notarized by a Latvian notary before registration with the Enterprise Register
Latvia.notes: The 2016 Nonprofit Organizations Law unified the forms; the notary step forces an in-person visit or a local representative, which is the main barrier for a foreign founder

Lithuania.entity_types: Nonprofit organization (NVO), public benefit institution (viešoji įstaiga), foundation
Lithuania.cost_time: State fee ~€20–50 (plus notary if offline); ~3–10 business days
Lithuania.requirements: Lithuanian address, Lithuanian-language name and documents; NVO needs a board and min. 1–2 founders; registration via e-signature or notary with the Register of Legal Entities
Lithuania.notes: The fully online route requires a Lithuanian e-ID, so a foreign founder usually acts through a local notary or representative; otherwise the process is fast

Netherlands.requirements: No citizenship/residency requirement for founder or board; 1+ board member (stichting), Dutch registered office (virtual office acceptable), ANBI declaration to Belastingdienst
Netherlands.notes: Most popular EU route for foreign founders; stichting + ANBI is the standard expat-charity path; board may be entirely non-resident; English-language guidance available; no minimum endowment

Belgium.requirements: Belgian registered office (seat must be in Belgium); association requires 1+ founder (since 2024 reform), 3+ traditionally; foundation requires EUR 25,000 minimum capital; French/Dutch-language statutes
Belgium.notes: ASBL is the standard vehicle and easy via a local registered-office provider; AIT tax-exempt status is a separate application; French-speaking practice dominates; no in-person steps required

Luxembourg.entity_types: Association (1912 law), Fondation (2003 law), European non-profit association (ENPA)
Luxembourg.cost_time: EUR 200-600 for association, 1-4 weeks; foundation several months (Tribunal authorisation)
Luxembourg.requirements: Luxembourg registered office; association needs 3+ founding members; foundation requires EUR 100,000 minimum endowment (Art. 40(3)) and court authorisation; English widely accepted
Luxembourg.notes: Most English-friendly EU jurisdiction; charitable income exempt from tax; foundation route is capital-heavy, association is the practical expat choice

France.entity_types: Association loi 1901, Fonds de dotation, Fondation reconnue d'utilité publique
France.cost_time: Association: free (déclaration), 1-2 weeks; fonds de dotation: EUR 15,000 endowment + EUR 300-500 filing
France.requirements: Association needs 2+ named founders (practically a president + 1 officer), French registered office; fond de dotation requires EUR 15,000 minimum endowment; French-language declaration at préfecture
France.notes: Association 1901 is quick and free; tax-exempt status (Art. 64 ter CGI) is complex and separate; French required in practice; public-utility recognition requires ~EUR 1M endowment and decree

Germany.entity_types: Eingetragener Verein (e.V.), Gemeinnützige gGmbH, Private foundation (Stiftung, state law)
Germany.requirements: e.V. needs 7+ founding members, German registered office (Geschäftssitz in Germany), German-language articles; foreign founders/directors allowed without residency proof
Germany.notes: e.V. is the standard vehicle; charity status (gemeinnützig) confirmed later by Finanzamt; state register courts are slow; foundation endowments vary by state from ~EUR 10,000-25,000

Austria.entity_types: Eingetragener Verein (Verein), Private foundation (Stiftung, state-level law)
Austria.requirements: Verein needs 3+ founders, Austrian seat (local address), Austrian-language articles; no citizenship requirement for founders or board
Austria.notes: Verein is the practical vehicle; foundation laws are state-by-state (Landesrecht) with endowments from ~EUR 30,000-75,000; German required; charity tax recognition via Finanzamt

Switzerland.cost_time: Foundation: CHF 50,000 endowment + CHF 1,000-2,000 registration, 4-8 weeks; association: CHF 500-1,000, 1-4 weeks
Switzerland.requirements: Foundation requires CHF 50,000 minimum capital, Swiss seat, 3+ foundation council members with at least 1 Swiss-domiciled; association needs 3+ founders and a Swiss board seat
Switzerland.notes: No citizenship requirement for founders; Swiss-resident officer is the key hurdle (use local agent); trilingual; neutral-content requirement for foundations; no formal 'charity' register - exemption via tax authority

Liechtenstein.requirements: Foundation requires CHF 30,000 minimum endowment, seat in Liechtenstein, managing board seated locally (local officer/agent needed); German-language filings
Liechtenstein.notes: Small, stable, English-tolerant jurisdiction; local board presence makes it impractical without a local agent; no formal charity register; often paired with Swiss structures

Monaco.requirements: Foundation requires EUR 50,000 minimum endowment and discretionary decree of the Prince on advice of the foundations commission; Monégasque registered office; French-language filings
Monaco.notes: No formal charity category - establishment is discretionary sovereign approval; French required; popular with high-net-worth founders; no corporate income tax; in-person steps common

San Marino.requirements: San Marino registered office; Italian-language filings; small opaque bureaucracy with in-person steps; endowment set by founding act for foundations
San Marino.notes: Tiny jurisdiction with few foreign precedents and no English-language service; most foreigners use a neighbouring Italian (Emilia-Romagna) association instead; Italian required

Andorra.requirements: Foundation requires endowment of at least EUR 100,000 per founding act, Andorran seat, local management presence; Catalan/Spanish-language filings, notarised documents
Andorra.notes: Popular with affluent founders seeking a European low-tax base; high endowment and local-presence requirements make it hard for a remote foreign founder; Catalan required in practice

Poland.entity_types: fundacja (foundation), stowarzyszenie (association), public benefit organization (pożytk pożyteczna organizacja, POUS)
Poland.cost_time: ~500-1,500 PLN notary + small fees; ~2-4 weeks (statutory 30 days)
Poland.requirements: Fundacja needs only 1 founder (foreigners allowed, no citizenship requirement), a notarized deed and a local registered office; association needs 7+ members.
Poland.notes: Most expat-friendly route in the region; separate 'benefit organization' (OPP) listing gives charity tax benefits; good English-language legal market.

Czechia.entity_types: spolek (association), obecně užitečná korporace (OUK, public benefit corporation), nadace (foundation)
Czechia.cost_time: Spolek: registration free + notary ~1,000-2,500 CZK; ~4-8 weeks; OUK faster (~2-4 weeks)
Czechia.requirements: Spolek needs 5+ members (foreigners allowed), a local registered office; OUK needs 1 founder, ~100,000 CZK endowment, notary deed; Czech-language statute.
Czechia.notes: Digital registry, straightforward; public-benefit (obecně prospěšná) tax status is a separate Ministry of Interior approval.

Slovakia.entity_types: nezisková organizácia (nonprofit organization), verejne prospešná organizácia (VPO), nadácia (foundation)
Slovakia.requirements: Organization needs 2+ founders, local office and Slovak-language charter; foundation via notarized deed, endowment per charter; no citizenship requirement.
Slovakia.notes: VPO public-benefit status is a separate Ministry of Interior procedure; Slovak language barrier; paperwork moderate.

Hungary.entity_types: civil nonprofit szervezet (civil nonprofit organization), nonprofit kft (nonprofit limited company), alapítvány (foundation)
Hungary.cost_time: Nonprofit org: low/no state fee + notary ~30,000-60,000 HUF, ~2-4 weeks; nonprofit kft needs 3,000,000 HUF capital
Hungary.requirements: Nonprofit organization needs 2+ members (foreigners allowed); foundation 1 founder + charter, Hungarian-language deed, local office.
Hungary.notes: Foreign-funded NGOs above a threshold (~300M HUF/yr) need government authorization (Stop-Soros legacy) — politically sensitive; public-benefit (közhasznú) status is a separate, stricter regime.

Slovenia.cost_time: Association ~200-500 EUR, ~1-2 months; foundation ~1,000-3,000 EUR, ~1-3 months
Slovenia.requirements: Association 3+ members (foreigners allowed), local office, Slovenian-language charter; foundation 1 founder, endowment per charter.
Slovenia.notes: Public-benefit (javno koristno) status is a separate procedure with membership-base criteria; English support limited outside Ljubljana.

Croatia.entity_types: udruga (association, javno korisna status), zakladnica (foundation), neprofitna ustanova (nonprofit institution)
Croatia.cost_time: ~500-1,500 HRK fees + notary; ~1-3 months (statutory 30 days, often longer)
Croatia.requirements: Udruga needs 3+ founding members (foreigners allowed), local office, Croatian-language statutes, notarized application in 2 copies.
Croatia.notes: EU e-government decent; javno korisna (public-benefit) status is a separate Ministry of Interior step; many expats use a local legal/NGO-service provider.

Bosnia & Herzegovina.cost_time: ~100-300 BAM (very low); ~2-6 weeks per tier, can stretch to months
Bosnia & Herzegovina.requirements: 3+ founders, local office, charter in local language; registration happens at entity level (Republika Srpska vs Federation of BiH), sometimes municipal, so structure depends on where the office is.
Bosnia & Herzegovina.notes: Three-layer state/entity system creates duplicated paperwork; no online registry; English support rare; foreign founders allowed but bureaucracy heavy.

Serbia.entity_types: udruženje građana (citizens' association), fundacija (foundation), neprofitna ustanova (nonprofit institution)
Serbia.requirements: Association needs 3+ founders (foreigners allowed), local office, Serbian-language charter; foundation 1 founder, endowment per charter.
Serbia.notes: Non-EU; English support limited; cheap registration; foreign founders routinely register (many Serbian diaspora do this); apostille for foreign ID documents.

Montenegro.requirements: Association 3+ founders (foreigners allowed), local office, Montenegrin-language charter; no online registry, in-person/notarized steps.
Montenegro.notes: Slow bureaucracy, documents in Montenegrin, minimal English support; EU-candidate so framework is straightforward in principle.

North Macedonia.requirements: Association 3+ founders (foreigners allowed), local office, Macedonian-language charter; low fees.
North Macedonia.notes: EU candidate, cheap and low-bureaucracy; language barrier for a resident-in-Australia founder means using a local agent/lawyer.

Albania.requirements: Association 3+ founders (foreigners allowed), local office, Albanian-language charter; new 2021 electronic register accepts applications by post/courier.
Albania.notes: 2021 NPO registration law modernized the register; English support limited; foreign-founded NGOs common, often with local partners.

Moldova.requirements: Association 3+ founders (foreigners allowed), local office, Romanian-language charter (Russian widely used in practice); foundation 1 founder, endowment per charter.
Moldova.notes: Cheap; EU candidate; political/economic volatility and weak enforcement; banking for foreign directors can be fiddly.

Ukraine.entity_types: publichna organizatsiia (public organization), fundatsiia (foundation), publichno-koristna (public-benefit) status
Ukraine.cost_time: State duty ~1,000-2,500 UAH + translations/notary; ~1-2 weeks (online filing)
Ukraine.requirements: Organization 2+ founders (foreigners allowed), local office, Ukrainian-language documents (English with certified translation); state-fee registration online.
Ukraine.notes: Registration itself is cheap and fast, but active war, banking/sanctions friction for a foreign resident founder and currency risk make this a risky base; many Western expat charities run via local Ukrainian partners.

Belarus.cost_time: Nominally low fees, 1-3 months; in practice effectively barred for an independent foreign founder
Belarus.requirements: Nominally 5+ members for an organization (foreigners allowed in statute), local office, Belarusian-language charter; in practice foreign-funded NGOs above a funding threshold must register as 'undesirable organizations' before operating.
Belarus.notes: 2021+ crackdown on independent civil society; heavy political risk; private foundations rare and state-dominated; not recommended for this founder.

Romania.cost_time: ~500 RON state fee + notary ~1,000-2,000 RON; ~1-3 months (statutory 30 days)
Romania.requirements: Association 3+ founders (foreigners allowed), local office, Romanian-language statute; foundation 1 founder, endowment per charter, notary deed.
Romania.notes: EU member; moderate bureaucracy; 'de utilitate publică' (public-benefit) tax status is a separate, stricter procedure; English support OK in Bucharest/Cluj.

Bulgaria.entity_types: shtoprofitna asotsiia (public-benefit association), neprofitna pravno lice (nonprofit legal entity), fondatsiya (foundation)
Bulgaria.requirements: Nonprofit legal entity (NPL) needs only 1 founder (foreigners allowed) + local office; association needs 5+ founders; Bulgarian-language documents.
Bulgaria.notes: EU member; the 1-founder NPL form is the simplest for a lone foreign founder; good English support in Sofia; cheap to operate.

Greece.requirements: Association needs 5+ founders (foreigners allowed), Greek registered office, Greek-language charter filed with notary and court registry; foundation 1 founder, endowment per charter, notary deed.
Greece.notes: 2019 law modernized foundations, but process is paper/notary-heavy, Greek language required, no meaningful online registry; use a local lawyer.

Cyprus.entity_types: charitable trust (unregistered), registered body (association), community chest
Cyprus.cost_time: Trust: ~500-2,000 EUR via solicitor, days; registered body: ~100-500 EUR, ~2-6 weeks
Cyprus.requirements: A charitable trust needs only a settlor + trustee and no registration; registered body needs 3+ members (foreigners allowed) + local address; English fully accepted.
Cyprus.notes: English common-law jurisdiction — most expats set up a simple charitable trust with a Cypriot trustee; tax deductibility requires income-tax authority approval and a Cypriot public-benefit nexus; strong English-language professional services.

Malta.entity_types: association (2021 Non-Not-For-Profit Organisations Act), foundation, charitable trust
Malta.cost_time: Association ~150-500 EUR, ~days-2 weeks (online); foundation ~1,500-5,000 EUR, ~2-6 weeks
Malta.requirements: Association 3+ founders (foreigners allowed), local registered address; foundation 1 founder, endowment per charter, notary deed; English fully accepted.
Malta.notes: English official language, streamlined 2021 framework; foundation is the stronger form for asset-holding; charitable trusts available under trust law without registration.

Spain.entity_types: Fundación (private foundation), Asociación (unincorporated association), plus limited charitable societies (SL/SA with statutory purpose)
Spain.cost_time: €1,500–€3,500 total (notary, registry, legal fees); ~1–3 months including regional foundation registry
Spain.requirements: Spanish registered office (domicilio social), Spanish-resident legal representative (representante legal), notarial deed of incorporation, and a minimum endowment of ~€30,000 for a fundación
Spain.notes: Foreign founders can establish a fundación without Spanish nationality or tax residency; the practical hurdle is appointing a resident legal representative and local office (via a Spanish firm/registered agent). Fundaciones register in the regional f

Portugal.entity_types: Fundação (private foundation, public-interest institution), Associação (association), and Instituto (institute)
Portugal.cost_time: €1,000–€2,500 (notary, legal, fees); ~1–2 months for notarisation and public-interest status
Portugal.requirements: Portuguese registered office and a locally-based responsible party/director; the foundation deed (estatutos) must be notarised; no statutory minimum endowment, but the granting authority can require a material contribution sufficient for the object t
Portugal.notes: The most straightforward of the four for a foreign founder: no citizenship/residency requirement for the founder, and no fixed minimum capital. However, to be treated as an entity of public interest (required for tax-exempt status and grants) it need

Italy.entity_types: Fondazione (private foundation), Associazione (unincorporated association), and cooperative sociale (social cooperative)
Italy.cost_time: €3,000–€6,000 professional costs plus the €150,000 endowment; ~2–4 months for notarisation, court filing and RUNTS entry
Italy.requirements: Italian registered office, a founder who may be foreign (no citizenship/residency requirement), and a minimum endowment of €150,000 (fully paid at formation) for a fondazione; registration in the Third-Sector National Register (RUNTS)
Italy.notes: Foreign (including Australian) founders can legally establish a fondazione — explicitly no nationality or residency requirement — but the €150,000 fully-contributed endowment is the main barrier and makes it one of the costlier routes. Charitable sta

Vatican City.entity_types: No ordinary commercial/charitable registry; charitable activity is conducted through pontifical institutions, canonically erected entities, or bodies recognised by the Holy See (e.g., pontifical foundations/works) rather than a self-service registrat
Vatican City.cost_time: No fixed fee or standard timeline; entirely case-by-case at the discretion of the Holy See
Vatican City.requirements: No independent self-registration pathway; any entity operating on Vatican territory must be recognised/erected by the Holy See (competent dicastery/pontifical authority) and be compliant with the Fundamental Law of the Vatican City State
Vatican City.notes: The Vatican does not operate a conventional commercial-law or charity-registration framework open to foreign founders. There is no public registry an Australian-resident can simply file into. Charitable or philanthropic activity on Vatican territory

Canada.entity_types: Federal registered charity (CRA), incorporated charity (Canada Not-for-Profit Corporations Act), charitable trust
Canada.cost_time: C$300 (C$100–200 incorporation + C$100 charity registration); incorporation 2–4 weeks, charity registration 35 days–3 months
Canada.requirements: No citizenship requirement for trustees, but a Canadian address must be maintained for records and filings (a registered agent suffices).
Canada.notes: English/French; no foreign-formation ban; popular with diaspora and dual-citizen charities; ongoing CRA reporting obligations are substantial.

United States.entity_types: State nonprofit corporation (e.g., Delaware, California), private charitable trust, 501(c)(3) tax-exempt organization
United States.cost_time: US$100–500 state filing + US$400–600 IRS Form 1023 fee; incorporation days–2 weeks, 501(c)(3) determination 6–12 months
United States.requirements: Registered agent and state address in the state of incorporation; no residency requirement for directors; English.
United States.notes: The most common foreign-founder pathway: state nonprofit corporation + 501(c)(3); fully remote; no charity regulator, only tax-exempt status.

Cuba.entity_types: None — no private charitable sector; state-affiliated solidarity funds only
Cuba.requirements: No charitable registration is open to foreign nationals; all civil-society bodies must be state-sanctioned.
Cuba.notes: Foreign formation is effectively barred; use a Canada/US entity and partner with a local state-linked body instead.

Jamaica.entity_types: Company limited by guarantee, charitable trust (deed), nonprofit corporation
Jamaica.requirements: Jamaican registered office and local company secretary/agent; no citizenship requirement for directors; English.
Jamaica.notes: No formal charity status, regulator, or donation tax-deductibility regime; most foreign founders use a company limited by guarantee + local manager.

Bahamas.entity_types: Company limited by guarantee (Companies Act, 2019), charitable trust, nonprofit society
Bahamas.requirements: Bahamas registered office and licensed registered agent; no residency requirement for directors; English.
Bahamas.notes: Strong offshore-agent ecosystem; no income tax so no tax-exempt registration is needed; donations are not tax-deductible for donors.

Barbados.entity_types: Company limited by guarantee (Companies Act, 2016), charitable trust
Barbados.requirements: Local registered office + agent; no citizenship requirement for directors; English.
Barbados.notes: No dedicated charity regulator; standard expat path is a company limited by guarantee with a local secretary.

Trinidad & Tobago.entity_types: Company limited by guarantee (Companies Act, 2019), charitable trust, society
Trinidad & Tobago.requirements: T&T registered office + local agent; no resident-director requirement; English.
Trinidad & Tobago.notes: Gifts to approved charitable organizations are income-tax deductible (T&T Income Tax Act); no formal charity status beyond government approval.

Antigua & Barbuda.entity_types: Company limited by guarantee (Companies Act), charitable trust
Antigua & Barbuda.requirements: Local registered office + registered agent; no residency requirement for directors; English.
Antigua & Barbuda.notes: Established offshore-agent services make remote formation straightforward; no charity tax regime.

Grenada.entity_types: Company limited by guarantee (Companies Act), charitable trust
Grenada.requirements: Local registered office + agent; no residency requirement for directors; English.
Grenada.notes: Agent services in English; little charity-specific legislation; company limited by guarantee is the standard vehicle.

St. Kitts & Nevis.entity_types: Company limited by guarantee (Companies Act), charitable trust
St. Kitts & Nevis.requirements: Local registered office + registered agent; no residency requirement for directors; English.
St. Kitts & Nevis.notes: Strong offshore-agent infrastructure; remote formation in English is practical.

St. Lucia.entity_types: Company limited by guarantee (Companies Act, 2015), charitable trust
St. Lucia.requirements: Local registered office + agent; no residency requirement for directors; English.
St. Lucia.notes: Agent services available; no charity regulator; English-language filings.

St. Vincent & Grenadines.entity_types: Company limited by guarantee (Companies Act), charitable trust
St. Vincent & Grenadines.requirements: Local registered office + agent; no residency requirement for directors; English.
St. Vincent & Grenadines.notes: Agent services in English; minimal charity-specific legislation; company limited by guarantee is the standard form.

Dominica.entity_types: Company limited by guarantee (Companies Act), charitable trust
Dominica.requirements: Local registered office + agent; no residency requirement for directors; English.
Dominica.notes: Offshore-agent ecosystem; English; no formal charity status.

Dominican Republic.requirements: Notarial deed (acta notarial) — in person or via apostilled special power — local seat and local fiscal; Spanish-language documents.
Dominican Republic.notes: Spanish bureaucracy; the notarial deed (in person or certified power of attorney) is the main hurdle; Chamber of Commerce registration and RNC tax ID required.

Haiti.entity_types: Declared association (association déclarée, Law No. 30 of 1943), NGO branch/representative office
Haiti.requirements: Founding deed before a Haitian notary, physical seat in Haiti, local legal representative/director; French.
Haiti.notes: French-language notarial deed plus registration with the public prosecutor; a local partner is effectively required; high security/political risk.

Mexico.requirements: 3+ founders, notarized Spanish-language articles, Mexican legal address; no citizenship requirement, then SAT RFC registration.
Mexico.notes: Donataria autorizada (DA) status with SAT is a separate multi-month step required for tax-deductible donations; English-speaking notary/lawyer services readily available in Mexico City.

Guatemala.entity_types: asociación sin fines de lucro; fundación; fideicomiso (trust)
Guatemala.requirements: Notarized Spanish articles, Guatemalan legal address, Registro de Comercio filing; foreign founders permitted.
Guatemala.notes: No dedicated charity registry or donor tax-benefit regime; notary and registry processes are slow; everything in Spanish.

Belize.entity_types: non-profit company (limited by guarantee); registered charity (Charities Act 2020); trust
Belize.requirements: 2+ directors (foreigners OK, no residency requirement), local registered office and company secretary via local agent; documents in English.
Belize.notes: English-speaking, simple Companies Registry; most expats form the non-profit company first and add charity registration later; local service providers handle everything.

El Salvador.entity_types: asociación sin fines de lucro; fundación (Ley 2011); fideicomiso (trust)
El Salvador.requirements: Spanish-language articles, local address, registry filing under the 2011 Associations and Foundations Law; foreign founders permitted.
El Salvador.notes: Donor tax benefits are limited; NGOs receiving international funds should also register in the Ministry of Foreign Affairs NGO directory.

Honduras.requirements: Spanish articles, local registered office, Registro de Personas Morales plus Registro de ONGD (Chancillería) filing for NGOs.
Honduras.notes: International ONGDs must register in the Registro Público de ONGD; moderate bureaucracy; all filings in Spanish.

Nicaragua.requirements: Spanish articles, local address, Registro Nacional filing; formally open to foreign founders.
Nicaragua.notes: Avoid: government has dissolved 5,700+ NGO legal personalities since 2018, including foreign-funded ones; laws target foreign-financed civil society, so an Australian-founded charity faces extreme cancellation/political risk.

Costa Rica.entity_types: asociación o fundación sin fines de lucro (single law); fideicomiso (trust)
Costa Rica.requirements: Notarized Spanish articles, local registered office, Registro de Comercio; 3+ members for an asociación, single founder for a fundación.
Costa Rica.notes: Stable, professional services widely available in English; donor tax exemption requires separate Ministry of Finance (MINFIN) approval.

Panama.entity_types: fundación de interés privado (FIP); asociación; fideicomiso (trust)
Panama.requirements: Spanish articles and name, local registered office, board of 3+ members, IFPF registration; single foreign founder permitted, no local nationals required.
Panama.notes: The FIP (Ley No. 8 de 2000) is the most popular expat foundation vehicle in Latin America; IFPF is a specialized fast registry; strong English-language support.

Colombia.entity_types: Fundación (private foundation), Asociación (incorporated association), Corporación (2016 hybrid)
Colombia.requirements: No nationality requirement for board; Colombian registered address, Colombian lawyer to execute the public deed and register with the Cámara de Comercio; filings in Spanish.
Colombia.notes: Most expat-friendly in the region; foreigners can be president/directors; Bogotá has strong English-speaking legal market; donation tax deductions require separate DIAN certification; 2023 NGO-law reforms (Ley 2287/2022) added transparency reporting

Venezuela.requirements: Local (Venezuelan) resident officers and registered office, Venezuelan lawyer, notarized deed; severe currency controls (CADIVI/SICR) on bank accounts and foreign donations.
Venezuela.notes: Major political/economic risk; 2010 Ley de ONGs lets the state restrict entities; foreign funding heavily scrutinized; most international NGOs operate through foreign legal entities, not Venezuelan ones.

Ecuador.entity_types: Fundación (private foundation), Asociación civil (incorporated association), Institución de utilidad pública (IUP, public-benefit institution)
Ecuador.requirements: Minimum 3 founders; Ecuadorian resident president/board and local address; Ecuadorian lawyer; 2023 reform (Ley 2023-13 / COEP regime) added registration and foreign-funding reporting obligations.
Ecuador.notes: Foreign founders permitted as members/board; Spanish-language documents; IUP status adds time and a public-benefit declaration; banking and tax (SRI) onboarding is slow.

Peru.entity_types: Asociación civil (civil association), Fundación (private foundation), Instituto (non-profit institute)
Peru.requirements: Public deed registered with SUNARP; local registered office; president/legal rep should be resident in Peru for banking; filings in Spanish.
Peru.notes: No nationality requirement; foreign founders allowed; tax exemption (exoneración) from SUNAT is separate, discretionary and needs annual reporting; Lima is the practical hub; English not official.

Bolivia.requirements: Resident (Bolivian) officers, local address, notarized deed; 2023 NGO law (Ley 1417, replacing 1993 Ley 1475) requires registration and restricts foreign funding, advocacy and political activity of foreign-funded entities; Spanish only.
Bolivia.notes: Foreign NGOs must register with the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Cancillería); 2023 law caps foreign government funding for certain activities and tightens oversight; heavy Spanish-language bureaucracy; few English speakers.

Guyana.entity_types: Non-profit company (NPC, 2018 Act), Friendly society (Friendly Societies Act), Co-operative society
Guyana.requirements: Guyanese registered office and resident directors; English is official; no citizenship requirement for board but a local presence is needed; no restrictions on foreign donations.
Guyana.notes: Easiest bureaucracy in the sub-region and English-speaking; non-profits face extra scrutiny at formation and take longer than companies; tax exemption is discretionary (Commissioner of Inland Revenue); friendly societies are the most common non-profi

Suriname.requirements: Surinamese notary (deeds in Dutch), local board/office in practice; 2013 Dutch-style Civil Code permits stichting with foreign elements but a local notary and presence are required in practice; Dutch language barrier.
Suriname.notes: Dutch is the working language — the main barrier; small legal market; banking requires a local presence; few English-speaking professionals; new Civil Code (in force 2013) modernized foundation law but practice is conservative.

Brazil.entity_types: Associação (association), Fundação (private foundation), OSC/OSCIP (social organization, Law 9.093/1995)
Brazil.requirements: Minimum 2 members (association) or 1 founder (foundation); Brazilian CNPJ and local address; notarial deed registered with a cartório; foreign founder may join the board; filings in Portuguese.
Brazil.notes: Heavy red tape (famous bureaucracy); main hurdles are getting a CPF and a bank account (foreign-inflow/câmbio rules); OSCIP certification gives donation tax deductions; 'instituição de utilidade pública' (federal/municipal) is a long, discretionary e

Paraguay.entity_types: Fundación (private foundation), Asociación civil (civil association), Cooperativa (cooperative)
Paraguay.requirements: Local registered office and a local representative; notarized deed; founder may be foreign; registration with the relevant ministry/civil registry; Spanish documents.
Paraguay.notes: Under-regulated and relatively tolerant of foreign founders, but the legal market is small and Spanish-only; tax exemption requires separate certification; fewer English-speaking lawyers than neighboring countries; slower administration than Chile/Ar

Uruguay.entity_types: Asociación (association), Fundación (private foundation, public or private interest)
Uruguay.requirements: Minimum 3 persons (association); local registered office; foundation requires a local representative; registration with the Registro Nacional de Personas Jurídicas; Spanish filings.
Uruguay.notes: Very stable, low political risk; foundations enjoy tax incentives (50% exemption on qualifying income); English reasonably available in Montevideo business circles; 'declaración de utilidad pública' optional.

Argentina.entity_types: Asociación civil (civil association, Ley 23.851), Fundación (private foundation, Ley 27.290/2016), Cooperativa (cooperative)
Argentina.requirements: Local registered office and resident director/legal rep; foreign founder/trustees allowed; notarial deed registered with the commercial registry (personas jurídicas); Spanish filings.
Argentina.notes: Most expat-friendly bureaucracy in South America; English widely spoken in Buenos Aires; foreign founders can serve on boards; donation tax exemption is a separate AFIP step ('Ingreso a Régimen de Entidades Exentas', Ley 24.976); 2016 foundation law

Chile.entity_types: Asociación (association), Corporación (corporation), Fundación de derecho privado (private foundation, Ley 20.839/2015)
Chile.requirements: Chilean registered office; board may include foreigners; legal representative should be resident in Chile; public deed registered with the Conservador de Bienes Raíces; Spanish filings.
Chile.notes: Fast, clean bureaucracy; the de facto hub for LATAM expats and many run foundations/associations there; English widely used in Santiago legal market; donor tax deduction requires 'calificación' from the tax authority; 2015 law modernized foundations.

North Korea.entity_types: state-run public organization (no independent charitable sector)
North Korea.requirements: no meaningful independent charity registration; foreign involvement barred in practice
North Korea.notes: No independent charitable pathway; no GfN. Excluded from any practical plan.

Russia.entity_types: public organization (NGO) / public foundation registered with Ministry of Justice
Russia.requirements: Russian-language filings, foreign-agent law risks for foreign-linked orgs, sanctions on AU side
Russia.notes: No GfN. Sanctions + foreign-agent regime make this unsuitable for an Australian founder.
